motion: Does the historical evidence of suffering justify confidence in the sincerity of all the original resurrection witnesses?

bridges.description: Connect continued public commitment under expected suffering to the probability of sincere resurrection belief.
Combine unequal martyrdom evidence, collective testimony, and persecution patterns without requiring identical evidence for every witness.
Treat continued public association with a threatened movement as relevant even without individual preaching or a final recantation chance.
Test whether evidence about limited leaders justifies confidence about all original witnesses.
Separate death or persecution from proof that abandonment of the resurrection claim could have prevented it.
Require evidence before treating a flexible title or collective narrative as proof that each original witness preached and remained exposed.

moves.speaker: Trent Horn
moves.claim: The popular claim that every apostle was martyred overstates an evidential record that is much stronger for some witnesses than for others.
moves.warrant: Horn distinguishes his broader personal belief from evidence suitable for a skeptical audience.
moves.inference: The motion should rest on a cumulative, uneven case rather than an all-or-nothing martyrdom slogan.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This compact opening states Horn’s governing qualification and his move to willingness to suffer.

moves.audioVerificationReason: No direct audio verification has occurred; the non-mixed wording is coherent.

moves.speaker: Paulogia
moves.claim: Horn’s nuanced formulation is preferable, while stronger universal martyrdom claims require qualification.
moves.warrant: Paulogia contrasts Horn’s approach with the stronger tradition he received and explicitly appreciates the nuance.
moves.inference: The live dispute concerns what limited evidence can justify about all witnesses.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Preserves Paulogia’s concession and the background for his narrower challenge.
